keyFindings.description: `.replace("\\\n", " ")` joins backslash-continued lines before comments are stripped, so a comment ending in a backslash swallows the next line: `# keep the toolchain pinned \` then `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in envoy_plugin_publish's Push tag step (DEPLOY_KEY in its env) leaves the checker green while bash runs the install (a `#` comment ends at the newline; verified `printf '# c \\\necho RAN\n' | bash` prints RAN). An escaped trailing backslash (`printf 'x' \\` then `bun install`) is swallowed the same way. Before this push both shapes were caught. Fix: strip each line's comment before joining and join only a real continuation (`(?<!\\)\\\n`); two fixtures beside the existing backslash-continuation case.

The path and content checks run only inside `if [ "$parent" = "$upstream" ]`, so a doctored commit whose parent is an older main commit is refused only on attempt 2 after a rebase, and when main's manifest already holds the version or a later one the superseded-version exit (:490-503) drops it unchecked with exit 0 — nothing pushed, but §4 of the solution doc (:168-173) says 'refused rather than dropped'. Check against `$parent` before the `if` (identical to today's checks when parent == upstream) and add the stale-branch doctored case (2g) the header's 'checked again there' claims; or state the drop in §4.

`only_bump` ends 'HEAD's parent must be main's tip', which is not the rule (an older parent is rebased), and is appended to five refusals it does not explain; say what is enforced — main's manifest with .version = v$version and nothing else.

`job.lines["continue-on-error"]` is indexed directly where every other site uses `.lines.get(key, fallback)`, and the message states an effect ('reports a failed tripwire as success') that is false for `continue-on-error: false`; state the rule as the step-level sibling does.
NO_TARBALL says 'without a tarball argument' for `npm publish --access public x.tgz`, a legal order with the tarball present; name the rule ('the tarball must be the word right after publish').

§4's conclusion 'refused rather than dropped or pushed' overstates the superseded-version exit, which still drops a doctored commit unchecked (exit 0, nothing pushed); becomes true with the parent-side check above, else say so.
